title: Foreign Affairs Portfolio Miscellaneous Measures Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would create a transfer pathway from the Australian Secret Intelligence Service to public service agencies and permit tailored workplace safety declarations for intelligence work.
Service employees could move under the public service’s voluntary transfer process, and the Director-General could modify or disapply specified safety provisions with ministerial approval.
When administering the service and making declarations, the Director-General would have to consider workplace safety objectives so far as consistent with maintaining national security.
changes: Transferred intelligence employees would become public service employees for all purposes.
The Public Service Commissioner and Director-General would agree equivalent employee classifications.
Safety declarations could address particular workplaces, activities or categories of workers.
The changes would start on Royal Assent.
summary.affected: Intelligence service employees, receiving public service agencies and people working for the Director-General are affected.

speeches.speaker: Richard Marles
speeches.brief: Introduced the Foreign Affairs Portfolio Miscellaneous Measures Bill, which lets Australian Secret Intelligence Service employees transfer between public service agencies while protecting their identity, and gives the ASIS director general power to modify Work Health and Safety Act provisions with ministerial approval.

speeches.speaker: Julie Bishop
speeches.brief: Supported the Foreign Affairs Portfolio Miscellaneous Measures Bill, which lets ASIS employees transfer between public service agencies without disclosing their intelligence role, and gives the ASIS director general power to modify Work Health and Safety Act provisions, noting ASIS was established in 1952.

speeches.speaker: Richard Marles
speeches.brief: Summarised the Foreign Affairs Portfolio Miscellaneous Measures Bill's amendments to the Intelligence Services Act and Work Health and Safety Act, allowing ASIS employees to transfer between public service agencies while protecting their identities, and giving the ASIS director general power to modify safety act provisions with ministerial approval, matching arrangements already available to the Australian Defence Force and ASIO.
